key_insight: Cryogenic Raman signatures reveal local symmetry breaking in Cs₂SnI₆ without a global structural phase transition.
engineering_relevance: Understanding local distortions and anharmonic dynamics could inform the design of lead-free thermoelectric and optoelectronic materials.
method: Analysis of phonon intensities, energies, and spectral lineshapes
evidence_signal: Below 200 K, enhanced multi-phonon scattering and Raman-forbidden modes emerge, while phonon intensity trends yield a phenomenological Arrhenius activation energy of 15–20 meV.
watch_item: The Raman evidence supports local symmetry breaking but does not uniquely establish its microscopic origin or demonstrate improved device performance.
paper_title: Temperature-Dependent Raman Signatures of Local Symmetry Breaking in Vacancy Double Perovskite Cs$_2$SnI$_6$
